olivia_custsuccess: FYI — AcmeApps (acct acme-67) escalated an invoice mismatch. Invoice shows 3,210,412 tokens for Feb billing period but our dashboard shows 2,592,087. They say >90% of usage is streaming chat and they do short client-side cancels/reconnects. They suspect duplicate token counts when SSE reconnects. sample request id: 0a1b2c3d. Posting raw snippets from the customer and logs below.

acme_billing_contact_jane: we only abort the client (ctrl-c/abort) then reconnect a second later. we never resend the whole prompt — only resume chat. invoices jumped this month which triggered the escalation.

alex_support: can you paste the raw SSE fragments and any correlation ids? also include the SDK/version if possible.

acme_billing_contact_jane: here's the raw stream we captured (redacted IPs). note duplicate chunks after reconnect:
```
-- client SSE raw --
id: 0a1b2c3d
event: message
data: {"chunk_id":"c1","delta":"Hello, wor"}
data: {"chunk_id":"c2","delta":"ld!","done":false}
# client abort (SIGINT) at t=12.3s
# reconnect after 1.8s, server replays last fragments
data: {"chunk_id":"c1","delta":"Hello, wor"}
data: {"chunk_id":"c2","delta":"ld!","done":true}
```

acme_billing_contact_jane: we also attached the client abort stack (Node 18, fetch + AbortController). no retries in our code beyond the immediate reconnect.

alex_support: thanks. billing_ops_bot, can you look at commit events for request 0a1b2c3d? any duplicate token_commit events?

billing_ops_bot: Auto-check: found 2 token_commit events for request 0a1b2c3d on 2026-02-27T22:14:05Z and 2026-02-27T22:14:08Z. Token counts: first commit=4,812 tokens, second commit=4,812 tokens, total attributed=9,624 tokens. Possible duplicate commits from stream resume. Flagging for eng.

mike_eng_oncall: quick hypothesis: when client aborts, the runtime closes the transport but the billing pipeline may have already emitted a partial commit; on reconnect the runtime resumes and emits another commit for the overlapping fragments without de-dup. Repro steps that I used to reproduce locally:
```
# repro (Node)
const controller = new AbortController();
fetch("https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=chat-xyz", {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'x-redwood-req-id': '0a1b2c3d' },
  body: promptStream(),
  signal: controller.signal
});
setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 12300); // abort mid-stream
setTimeout(() => reconnectWithSameSession(), 14000); // reconnect quickly

# result: runtime emitted token_commit for fragments up to chunk c2 on abort, then again on reconnect when finalization happened. billing pipeline currently keys dedupe on request_id only, which doesn't prevent duplicate commits from resumed streams.
```

mike_eng_oncall: mitigation options:
- short-term: billing can dedupe token_commit events by (request_id, chunk_id) during reconciliation to avoid double-charge for this billing period (we can apply credits).
- mid-term: runtime should include a monotonic stream_seq or chunk_id that's persisted and billing should ignore replayed chunk_ids. we'll push a patch to include chunk-level IDs in commit events and update reconciliation logic.

billing_ops_bot: billing will prepare a pro-rated credit for acme-67 for the suspected duplicates once eng confirms the event list. please confirm the total duplicate tokens found so far (billing ops audit).

alex_support: acme_jane, would you accept a credit while engineering ships the fix?

acme_billing_contact_jane: yes, a credit is fine. please keep me posted and let me know if you need any more logs.

olivia_custsuccess: tagging this P2 and moving to eng-oncall + billing ops. mike, please post a short RFC for the chunk_id dedupe approach and an ETA for the patch. billing_ops_bot, please start the credit workflow.

mike_eng_oncall: will do — patch planned today, deploy to canary in ~6h, full rollout tomorrow. I'll post PR link in this thread.

alex_support: thanks everyone — I'll update the customer thread with the credit confirmation once billing completes. :thumbsup:
